subject: Brahmaputra River
hook: BRAHMAPUTRA RIVER IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Unlike most Indian rivers that have feminine names, the Brahmaputra has a rare male name
angle_support: "While most rivers on the Indian subcontinent have female names, this river has a rare male name."
"In its Tibetan and Indian names, the river is unusually masculine in gender."
title: Why the Brahmaputra Isn't Like Other Indian Rivers
description: Most Indian rivers carry feminine names, but the Brahmaputra stands out with a masculine title. Its name means "son of Brahma," highlighting a rare naming tradition in the subcontinent.
narration: BRAHMAPUTRA RIVER IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You assume Indian rivers are all named with feminine titles, like Ganga or Yamuna. The Brahmaputra breaks that pattern with a masculine name in Sanskrit, traditionally unlike others. Brahmaputra translates to 'son of Brahma' in Sanskrit—a masculine title. By contrast, major Indian rivers such as Ganga, Yamuna, Saraswati, Kaveri, and Godavari bear feminine names, making Brahmaputra a rare male‑named river in the entire subcontinent. A river named for a god’s son, not a goddess here.
